correctness.rationale: Variation of constants for \(\dot z+z=y^2\) gives the exact backward exponential memory on every bounded complete trajectory and proves nonnegative, and away from the origin strictly positive, height. Stationarity of \(xy\), together with \(\mathbb E[xy]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[y^2z]=\mathbb E[z^2]\), yields \(\operatorname{Var}(z)=m(b-m)+\mathbb E[x^2]\). Conditional orthogonality of \(\dot z=y^2-z\) gives the height-speed variance and covariance formulas. Vanishing of either defect forces compact complete support trajectories to be equilibria. The packaged checker independently verifies the algebraic identities.

value.rationale: In the Rucklidge model, \(y\) is the convective amplitude while \(z\) represents a horizontal-average temperature, so an exact relation between these variables is intrinsic to the physical model rather than an arbitrary statistic. The theorem upgrades the linear temperature equation into a complete bounded-history representation and an all-invariant-measures fiber calibration. More importantly, stationarity of the coupled \((x,y)\) subsystem produces a fixed-point chord whose excess is exactly transverse kinetic energy. For \(b>0\), this makes the fixed-point mixtures a sharp lower-variance boundary and proves that every genuinely recurrent stationary state must visit temperatures above the nonzero-equilibrium height. These give exact checks for periodic-orbit and chaotic-state computations in a model whose modern literature explicitly organizes chaos using the section \(z=b\).
